notes: Plain text abstracts only. All metrics derived from abstract-length text (30-294 words). Paragraphs fixed at 3 due to extraction format (metadata header + blank line + abstract body). These baselines establish the variance envelope for academic writing — not point estimates. The wide TTR and sentence-length ranges demonstrate why single-threshold detectors fail on this register.

type_token_ratio.note: Inversely correlated with word count — shorter abstracts naturally show higher TTR. Normalize by length before comparing.

avg_word_length.note: Academic writing skews longer due to technical vocabulary. Math/stats papers trend toward 5.8-6.4; CS/AI papers toward 5.0-5.5.

avg_words_per_sentence.note: High variance. Papers with formal logical exposition (e.g., paper #54 at 33.0 w/s) vs. papers with enumerated contributions (e.g., paper #10 at 7.8 w/s) represent fundamentally different rhetorical strategies within the same register.

variance_analysis.implication: Text-only signals have weak discriminative power for academic writing due to high intra-register variance. Forensic evidence (document construction patterns, metadata, revision history) is critical for reliable classification in this register.
